title: Querywise Fair Learning to Rank through Multi-Objective Optimization

problem.claim: Learning-to-Rank must jointly address relevant search results and fair exposure for items in a protected group, which can conflict.

gap.claim: Combining relevance and fairness through a single linear combination is limited by objective nonconvexity and can produce suboptimal relevance.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes using Multi-Objective Optimization algorithms for Fair Learning-to-Rank.
The authors extend multi-objective optimization to a querywise setting to reduce exposure disparity both on average and at the query level.
The method improves computational efficiency by using the Gumbel max trick to sample the Plackett-Luce distribution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: For moderate fairness requirements, the proposed approach improves ranking relevance instead of deteriorating it.
The authors attribute the relevance improvement to benefits of multi-task learning and report studying the effect of fair ranking on the relevance-ranking task.
Evaluation on three real-world datasets reportedly shows improved relevance ranking over state-of-the-art solutions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Relevance and fair exposure can conflict in Learning-to-Rank.
Prior linear-combination approaches are limited by nonconvex objectives and may reduce relevance.
The paper applies multi-objective optimization and extends it to querywise optimization.
The authors report improved relevance under moderate fairness requirements and connect this to multi-task learning.
The approach uses Gumbel-max sampling for efficiency and is evaluated on three real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: For moderate fairness requirements, the authors report improved relevance rather than deterioration.

interpretation.claim: Moderate fairness constraints can sometimes provide beneficial multi-task effects for relevance.

application.claim: Test fairness-relevance tradeoffs across a range of fairness requirements instead of assuming fairness always lowers relevance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether relevance improves outside the reported moderate-fairness regime.

unknowns: The abstract does not define the fairness and relevance metrics.
The abstract does not identify the three datasets or report quantitative results.
The abstract does not specify the compared state-of-the-art methods or computational measurements.
The abstract does not describe the multi-objective optimization algorithms or fairness-requirement range.
